summary: Added an independent from-scratch implementation of S021 (ORB / opening-range breakout on Nasdaq 100), built per claude/strategy-passport-S021.md sec 3 without access to the original Anton code at ~/Trading/strategies/ORB-intraday-momentum (not reachable from this session) -- the point was independent verification per the passport sec 0/9. Backtest against real data/histdata/DAT_ASCII_NSXUSD_M1_*.csv surfaced a material discrepancy: the passport claims "09:30-15:59 America/New_York, with DST" but its claimed numbers (1518 trades, 53.0% win rate, 8/8 positive years, +11.06 pt/trade) reproduce almost exactly only when histdata's raw fixed-EST (UTC-5, no DST) timestamps are treated as literal NY local time -- i.e. NOT DST-converted, matching the repo's established non-DST convention for this index source (scripts/convert_histdata_indices.py) rather than the passport's own stated spec. Running the identical frozen rules with a genuine DST-aware America/New_York conversion gives a materially different and weaker result (1712 trades, 8.71 pt/trade, only 5/8 positive years, maxDD -2352 vs claimed -2659). No Gate 3 (prop-firm) work started yet -- deferred pending Anton's decision on which session convention is canonical for S021.

Resolved the DST/session-anchor question from the earlier commit on this session_id: split both backtest runs (raw fixed-EST-clock vs true DST-aware NY local) by whether each trading day falls in EST or EDT, and found the two runs agree EXACTLY in EST months (603 trades, +12.75 pt/trade both) and diverge only in EDT months, where the fixed-EST-clock reading of "09:30" lands on true NY local 10:30 (one hour into the session) rather than the true 09:30 open. Discussed with Anton (chat, same date): this seasonal-conditional anchor (true open in winter, true 10:30 in summer) is the intended design going forward, not a bug to fix -- it is also simpler to run live since it needs no DST-aware timezone conversion at all, just the fixed-offset clock histdata/cTrader already give. Repointed engine.py's canonical load_nsxusd_m1() to NOT DST-convert (previously it did); renamed the old DST-aware loader to load_nsxusd_m1_true_dst_local() and kept it only as a diagnostic/reference implementation, not used by simulate(). Updated config.py's docstring/session_open comment to document the fixed-EST clock convention instead of claiming DST-aware NY wall-clock. Re-verified after the edit: simulate() now reproduces exactly the passport's claimed trade count and win rate (n=1518, win_rate=0.530); avg net pts/trade is 10.69 vs the claimed 11.06, a small residual gap most likely from minor unobserved details of Anton's original implementation.

Built Gate 3 (prop-firm survivability) simulation for S021, requested by Anton same-day chat ("что бектестить, особенно с учетом пропа"), after the session-anchor question was resolved. Adapted the block-bootstrap Monte Carlo methodology from backtest/run_s007_propscheme.py (same thresholds: cashout +9%, daily limit -3%, total DD -10%; BLOCK_LEN=5, T_MAX=500, N_SIM=4000) to S021's much simpler at-most-1-trade/day structure: R = net_pts / (stop_adr_mult * ADR14) per trade, one R value per valid trading day (0.0 on no-trade days), full calendar day sequence preserved (not signal-days-only) so trade frequency stays realistic inside each 5-day block. Ran FILL_PROB=1.0 (no measured S021 execution-degradation figure exists, unlike S007's stated 3-of-4 heuristic -- fabricating one would misrepresent an unmeasured quantity) and instead stress-tested cost sensitivity directly (1.0bp baseline vs 3.0bp, matching the passport's own cost-sensitivity finding). Key results: longest historical losing streak = 8 (matches the passport's claimed 8-in-a-row exactly, independent confirmation); because S021 allows only 1 trade/day, the daily -3% limit is structurally almost unbreachable up to ~2.5%/trade risk (single-trade max loss ~= risk_pct), unlike S007 which pyramids intraday -- total drawdown, not the daily limit, is the binding constraint for S021. At 0.50-0.75%/trade: ~91-92% cashout rate, 2-8% total-DD bust, near-zero timeout -- the best risk band found on the grid tested (0.10/0.25/0.50/0.75/1.00/1.50/2.00%). Stress scenario (3bp cost) still gives ~80% cashout at the same risk band. Full grid results in reports/s021_propscheme_summary.csv.

Fixed S021 live bot never placing an order: cTrader caps a trendbars response at ~14000 bars regardless of the requested window, so the 30-day M1 fetch covered only ~13 sessions and ADR14 (adr_window=14) was always NaN. ADR14 history is now fetched as M15 (CTraderORB._get_m15_step/get_m15, HISTORY_DAYS=30) in parallel with a small M1 'today' window (TODAY_M1_DAYS=3); run_live_cycle_orb/decide()/run_cycle_for_account gained the m15/today_days arguments, and _levels_for_today was split into _today_anchor/_valid_prior_sessions plus an M15 day-validity threshold _m15_min_session_bars (ceil(350*26/390)=24, via a local cfg.with_() copy -- frozen engine/config untouched). M15 session ranges were verified identical to M1 on all 1624 valid days of the NSXUSD histdata set; ceil rather than round was chosen because round (23) admitted 126 truncated DST-week sessions the backtest rejects, while ceil leaves one mismatch day (2026-04-28, missing exact 09:30 M1 bar). decide() now logs a WARNING 'insufficient_adr_history' event when the 09:30 anchor is valid but fewer than adr_window prior sessions are available, instead of collapsing it into has_levels=False.

Flipped S021's broker_mode from 'off' to 'execute' (account_strategy id=5, ctrader-47939312, env=demo) per Anton's explicit request ('пусть на аккаунте 007 торгует') -- it had been enabled=True since 2026-09-22 10:55 but broker_mode was never set past its BrokerMode.OFF default, so it had been ticking in pure shadow ('mode=shadow', actions=0 always) this whole time despite Anton believing it was already live. Done via a direct AccountStrategy.broker_mode ORM write (webapp.db session) -- no CLI command exists for this today (webapp/cli.py's link-strategy has no --broker-mode flag, and there is no separate update-account-strategy command; S009/S011 were apparently flipped the same manual-DB-write way historically). Since Account.env='demo' (not cTrader's 'live'), webapp/runner.py::_worker_orb's own allow_mainnet = (broker_mode=='execute' and acc.env=='live') gate stays False regardless -- orders will only ever reach the demo account, matching Anton's actual intent (trade on the S007 demo account) with no real-money exposure. Verified via the same gate logic already used by S011 (line ~406) and S009 (line ~325) in webapp/runner.py. Session window opens 17:00 Kyiv (14:00 UTC) today -- this is expected to actually place orders for the first time once it does. Worth adding a proper webapp/cli.py command for this (set-broker-mode or similar) instead of raw ORM writes each time -- not done here, flagging as a gap.

Two fixes for the 2026-09-24 S021 overnight-position incident (see this session's earlier entry on the incident itself), per Anton's explicit 2-part request: '1: закрывать позы на 10 минут раньше, 2: каждое утро проверять позы по ТС и закрывать если что-то пошло не так'. (1) bot/orb_config.py: added LIVE_EXIT_BUFFER_MIN=10 -- decide()'s live time-exit check (bot/orb_signals.py, case 3/4) now fires 10 minutes before strategies.orb_intraday.config::ORB_BASE.session_close (15:59 fixed-EST) instead of AT it, giving the cron window (ends 20:59 UTC = 15:59 fixed-EST) 10 one-minute cycles of slack to actually catch and execute the close instead of 0 (the exact gap that caused yesterday's incident: the last cycle of the day was 2 minutes short). Deliberately does NOT touch session_close itself -- that field is also read by the frozen backtest engine (strategies/orb_intraday/engine.py) and by decide()'s own ADR-session-validity threshold, neither of which should move (strategy-passport-S021.md sec 10: 'не переоптимизировать') -- this is a live-only operational safety margin, computed in minutes (no new datetime imports needed). 19/19 tests/bot/test_orb_*.py pass unchanged. (2) New scripts/position_audit.py: reads every open broker position via the existing CTraderS007/CTraderORB.open_positions()/close_position() methods (no new order-sending code -- reuses the same path the live strategies already use) and closes anything still open, for S007 (account_strategy id=1) and S021 (id=5) only -- explicitly rejects S009/S011 (SystemExit) since those are multi-day/portfolio strategies where an open position before session start is the NORMAL resting state, not a defect. Relies on a timing invariant instead of per-strategy timezone/date arithmetic: scheduled to run 5 minutes BEFORE each strategy's own session opens (see deployment/schedule.yml's two new task entries, s007_position_audit at 09:55 Kyiv and s021_position_audit at 13:55 UTC via tz:UTC), so 'any position still open at audit time' is stale by construction -- no label/date parsing needed, which sidesteps S007 (Europe/Bucharest-anchored labels) vs S021 (fixed UTC-5-anchored labels) using different date references. 4 new tests (tests/scripts/test_position_audit.py, DB and adapter classes monkeypatched, no real broker/DB touched): scope-guard rejection, clean state closes nothing, a stale S021 position gets closed, S007 uses the right adapter class. algo-worker:latest rebuilt (`podman compose build worker`) so both the exit-buffer fix and the new audit task are live from the next scheduled tick -- verified via full test suite (scheduler_tick + bot: 147/147 pass) before the rebuild.

Added the S021.1 'NAS100 Opening-Range Squeeze' preset (claude/strategies-registry.md S021.1, prompt P14) to this package as a default-off, additive extension -- strategy-modifiers discipline applied strictly. config.py: new fields on OrbConfig only (squeeze_preset_enabled=False default, orb_open_start/end=13:30/13:45 UTC, orb_entry_start/end=13:45/16:00 UTC, orb_force_close=20:00 UTC, orb_entry_buffer_pts=2.0, squeeze_atr_period=14, squeeze_atr_mult=0.7, trend_ema_period=50, orb_tp_r_mult=2.5) plus NAS_SQUEEZE_PRESET = ORB_BASE.with_(squeeze_preset_enabled=True); every existing OrbConfig field and ORB_BASE itself untouched. engine.py: appended ~230 lines below a clearly delimited marker comment -- nothing above that marker was edited. New sibling function simulate_squeeze_preset() (not a branch inside simulate()) plus its own helpers: load_nsxusd_m1_true_utc() (true-UTC loader via utils.histdata.load_histdata_m1_utc, distinct from this module's own load_nsxusd_m1() which stays on the fixed-EST-no-DST clock by design for the base engine), ema(), compute_daily_bars_utc(), compute_squeeze_filters() (Daily ATR14/EMA50 via utils.indicators.wilder_atr, shifted one day so a trading day only reads filters from strictly prior days), compute_orb_open_range() (a single M15 candle's high/low), and the SqueezeTrade dataclass + squeeze_trades_to_frame(). backtest/run_s021_squeeze_preset.py's run_regression_check() proves ORB_BASE/simulate() are unchanged byte-for-byte (n=1518, sum_net_pts=16220.614 exact match) before any preset result is reported -- a stronger, mechanically-enforced version of the usual code-comment verdict convention. Honest result: 1482 trades, win 22.7%, mean -0.346R@1bp, 0/8 years positive at any cost level (base ORB_BASE: 8/8) -- preset REJECTED, kept in the codebase per archive-don't-delete convention, verdict recorded in claude/strategy-passport-S021.md section 13 (not a separate passport). 13 new tests in tests/strategies/test_orb_squeeze_preset.py, all green on first run.

Anton's request ('let's test S007+S021 combo for prop, find the most profitable risk combination for passing challenges'): built a JOINT Gate 3 (prop-firm survivability) block-bootstrap Monte Carlo for S007+S021 running together on one account, reusing positions_matrix() from run_s007_propscheme.py and build_daily_R() from run_s021_propscheme.py. Key methodological point: samples ONE shared block-index sequence over the ALIGNED calendar-date axis (2023-06-26..2026-06-26, the intersection of both data windows) instead of bootstrapping each leg independently, so real joint day-to-day structure is preserved rather than assumed away. Daily R correlation S007-vs-S021 (zero-filled) = +0.0649 (near-zero). At the ACTUAL LIVE risk settings read from data/app.db (account_strategies: id=1 S007 risk_pct=0.25 preset=WORKING_S007_NEWSSAFE_MAX8_BE05_OFF2, id=5 S021 risk_pct=0.5, both broker_mode=execute on the same account_id=1): combo Gate 3 = 100.0% cashout / 0.0% daily-bust / 0.0% dd-bust / worst-day -2.92% (vs +9%/-3%/-10% thresholds), mean +0.293%/day -- strictly better cashout speed than either leg alone at the same risk (S007 solo 0.25%: 100% cashout, worst-day -2.60%; S021 solo 0.50%: 92.8% cashout). Sweep across S007 in {0.20,0.25,0.30}% x S021 in {0.25,0.50,0.75,1.00}% shows S021 can go up to 0.75% at S007=0.25% with only 99.7% cashout / 0.2% daily-bust (still negligible) for faster cashout (28 median days vs 30-39); pushing both legs higher (S007=0.30%, S021=1.00%) starts a real tradeoff (95.3% cashout / 4.5% daily-bust). Also found and flagged: claude/strategy-passport-S007.md sec 4d still says WORKING_S007_NEWSSAFE_MAX8(+BE) is 'candidate, not yet promoted' -- that's stale; the live bot has run the OFF2 evolution of that exact scheme for weeks (config.py's own PROMOTED 2026-09-02 / ALGODEV-43 comments confirm it, DB confirms it's executing). Full numbers: reports/s007_s021_combo_propscheme_summary.csv; narrative and recommendation: claude/decisions-log.md and claude/strategy-passport-S007.md/S021.md (Project docs, updated same session).

Anton's follow-up chain after the S007+S021 combo Gate 3 work: 'a my testirovali bu v 021?' (had breakeven ever been tested on S021 -- answer, after grepping the code, was no: S021 had no breakeven mechanism at all, unlike S007's live BE@0.5R) -> 'davai' (go ahead, implement and test it) -> 'proveri pri dostizhenii 0.5, 1, i 1.5 rr' (test specifically at 0.5R/1.0R/1.5R trigger levels). Implemented breakeven_at_r as a default-off OrbConfig field (None reproduces ORB_BASE exactly) plus three named presets ORB_BE05/ORB_BE10/ORB_BE15 via .with_() -- ORB_BASE and every existing OrbConfig field untouched, strategy-modifiers discipline applied strictly. engine.py's simulate() exit loop now tracks a current_stop that moves to entry_price once favorable excursion reaches breakeven_at_r * stop_dist ('breakeven' exit_reason, be_moved=True on the Trade dataclass); when breakeven_at_r is None the trigger stays None and the loop is provably a no-op, proven both by a byte-for-byte historical regression (n=1518, sum_net_pts=16220.614, matches the frozen baseline exactly) and by 6 new Gate 0 unit tests (tests/strategies/test_orb_breakeven.py: regression on an adversarial fixture that hits both the original stop and a BE trigger on the same bar, long/short arming+exit mechanics, the same-bar stop-assumed-hit-first tie-break, 'armed but not hit still runs to the real time exit', and a cross-day no-look-ahead check) -- all 6 passed on the first run, and the full pre-existing tests/strategies/ suite (137 tests) stayed green. New committed script backtest/run_s021_breakeven.py mirrors run_s007_breakeven.py's shape: Gate 0 regression -> Gate 1 backtest sweep (real 1bp cost, full 2019-2026 history) -> solo Gate 3 (reuses run_s021_propscheme.py's build_daily_R/prop_sim, same SEED) -> combo Gate 3 (reuses run_s007_s021_combo_propscheme.py's build_s007_frame/align/joint_prop_sim, same SEED, live risk settings S007=0.25%/S021=0.50%). HONEST RESULT: REJECTED at all three levels. Gate 1: BASE mean +0.0713R/trade WR 53.0% maxDD -17.09R (8/8 years+); BE@0.5R +0.0669R (-6.2%) WR 44.0% (-9pp) maxDD -18.65R (worse) -- clearly harmful; BE@1.0R +0.0704R (-1.3%) WR 51.8% maxDD -17.82R -- mildly negative; BE@1.5R +0.0714R (+0.1%, flat) WR 52.8% maxDD -16.09R (only mild DD improvement, armed on just 9.1% of trades and actually changes the exit on only 0.6%) -- essentially neutral. Gate 3 solo (0.50%/0.75% risk) and combo (S007+S021 joint, live settings) show cashout/bust rates within Monte-Carlo noise of the no-breakeven baseline at every level (solo cashout 89.5-91.9% across all 4 configs with no monotonic pattern; combo cashout 99.92-100%, busts ~0% everywhere) -- breakeven changes essentially nothing for prop-survivability, because S021's structural safety (1 trade/day, no pyramiding, no TP) already keeps the daily-loss lane closed regardless of where the stop sits intraday. Root cause (matches the hypothesis stated before implementing): S021 rides winners to the 15:59 time-exit with no TP, so cutting to breakeven on a pullback mostly just caps upside on trades that later recover and run, without protecting much on the loss side (bad days are usually the original stop hit outright, before ever reaching +R). Kept as documented off-by-default presets, not deleted, per archive-don't-delete convention. Verdict baked into config.py's breakeven_at_r field comment and the preset block comment (numbers + date, no 'once known' placeholder language left). No parameter search was run to rescue a positive result. Docs sync (claude/strategy-passport-S021.md, backtest-log.md, decisions-log.md) to follow in the Claude Project.

ALGODEV-61: S021 EA vs engine parity PASSES on the offline tester (NSXUSD_HD custom symbol, histdata 2025.03.01-2026.09.30, 574 EA days): exit code 0, 326 match / 198 ea_no_levels / 39 live_only_short_session / 11 both_no_trade, 0 failures. ALGODEV-61: CORRECTION -- the S021 session anchor was one hour late in BOTH live bots every US-DST month. histdata's NSXUSD M1 timestamps are true New York local time (DST-aware), not the fixed UTC-5 the repo assumed, so the engine's naive 09:30 reading has always been the real cash open, while bot/ctrader_orb.py converted broker UTC into Etc/GMT+5 and the EA used a fixed-offset clock -- both anchoring at 10:30 NY in summer.
